newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Grand Hotel says 96/97 outlook worse.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Grand Hotel says 96/97 outlook worse.

text.p: Grand Hotel Group said on Monday that its 1996/97 result was likely to be below the prospectus forecast if current trends continued.

The company, which listed on August 12 and operates the Grand Hyatt Melbourne and the Hyatt Regency Perth, also said its results in the final five months of calendar 1996 were likely to be in line with the prospectus.

"However, recently emerging developments are causing concern. If these trends continue, the group's performance for the ten and a half months to June 30 1997 is likely to be below the prospectus forecast," it said.

"The distribution for the period to 30/06/1997 was forecast to be 17 cents per share/unit (the equivalent of 19 cents per share/unit for a full 12 month period) and is now expected to be around 16 cents per share/unit," managing director Garry Cameron said.

Cameron said the negative developments were a lowering in forecast industry wide growth in room demand in both Victoria and Western Australia, aggressive room rate strategies by competitor hotels and the decision to accelerate renovations, especially hotel rooms, at both hotels.
